claims.statement: ReplaySource e SyntheticSource implement input point-in-time/replay versus seeded synthetic data; the source interface itself does not establish capture origin.
Statistical implementation documents Newey-West for inference, Holm for multiplicity, and block bootstrap for equity paths; promotion gate only recommends the existing phase.
Inference return adjustment uses one all-calls-known boolean, so one null cost disables subtraction for every consulted epoch; report cost gate remains unknown.
Real Jev run requires explicit paid-inference flag, call and USD caps, key and input-token price, then performs a preflight before shadow run.
Replay evidence always labels itself accounting-replay-only and keeps strategy qualification and financial authorization false.
Paper capital uses synthetic-paper mode and fixed false qualification/authorization fields; receipt settlement rejects unknown or incomplete cost.
Book-replay v4 acceptance remains proposed and unapproved, with fourteen implementation criteria not verified.

documentation_findings.statement: README.md:3 says SPEC, PLAN, and ACCEPTANCE were never versioned. The current paths are tracked and commit b7b4c6b (2026-10-12) added them in this folder. This does not disprove that the files at the former undefined path were untracked; clarify the intended referent rather than asserting a definite contradiction.
documentation_findings.action: Ask the integrator/owner to clarify the former path and chronology; leave proposal/unfrozen status intact.

documentation_findings.statement: The general lab guide implies per-epoch inference costs are subtracted when known; the real-Jev guide specifies subtraction only when every consultation cost is known. src/lab/run.ts matches the all-known rule, omitting known costs from all epochs if any cost is null.
documentation_findings.impact: The inference-cost gate remains unknown, so this cannot qualify the run; descriptive net returns may nevertheless be overstated for partial-cost runs.
documentation_findings.action: Decide desired accounting semantics, align both guides, and add a mixed-known/unknown cost regression before changing code.
